claims.text: Nanoscale compositional fluctuations create localized regions with altered lattice distortion in multi-component concentrated alloys.
These compositionally fluctuating regions are the primary mechanism governing alloy strength and deformation behavior.
Nanoscale compositional fluctuations pin dislocations and increase resistance to plastic flow.
Rapid quenching can produce a multi-component alloy with a near-uniform elemental distribution.
Controlled annealing and cooling can promote nanoscale compositional segregation without forming distinct secondary phases.
The proposed comparison can hold grain size and macroscopic segregation constant while changing nanoscale compositional segregation.
Nanoscale regions of altered composition and local atomic order induce lattice distortions.
Local compositional fluctuations generate heterogeneous elastic fields.
The heterogeneous elastic fields impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion increases yield strength.
Local compositional fluctuations affect strain-hardening behavior during deformation.
Samples with controlled nanoscale segregation will have higher yield strength than rapidly quenched, compositionally homogeneous samples.
Samples with controlled nanoscale segregation will exhibit greater strain hardening than the baseline samples.
Samples with controlled nanoscale segregation will exhibit a delayed onset of plastic deformation relative to the baseline samples.
The proposed mechanism applies only while compositional fluctuations remain nanoscale and substantial second-phase precipitation and grain growth are absent.
The dominance of nanoscale fluctuations over grain-boundary effects and macroscopic segregation may vary with alloy composition and processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The core prediction is conditional on the treatment actually producing nanoscale compositional fluctuations, but the falsification rule treats failure to detect those fluctuations together with unchanged properties as falsification. Failure to create the proposed mediator is a failed intervention rather than a decisive test of whether that mediator strengthens the alloy.
